name: WHIRL
summary: WHIRL observes a single human demonstration in an unstructured environment, uses hand and object tracking to build a prior over how the task should go, and then improves that prior through the robot's own real-world exploration. It ran across dozens of everyday tasks in real homes and offices — opening drawers, doors and fridges, taking out trash — with no task-specific robot demonstrations.
innovation: Human video used as a prior for exploration rather than as a direct supervision target, which sidesteps exact retargeting.
An agent that improves on hardware after watching, instead of requiring the human demonstration to be precisely imitable.
matters: Showed one-shot human observation plus practice can beat large teleoperation datasets on in-the-wild tasks.
limits: Needs real-world practice time for each new task, and the extracted priors are coarse.
lineage: The first practical human-video-to-robot pipeline that ran outside a lab.
